Editor's note: The first-person report and its judgments belong to the original Chinese author. This English rendition retains the opening essay, the full Day2 agenda including all eight roundtable descriptions, both keynote speakers, the complete attendee roster, and the registration details. Event dates, venue names, speaker titles, company names and personal names are source-attributed, not independently verified. The event described has already taken place (May 22, 2026); this is a historical backfill, not a current invitation. Monetary figures, audience claims and company descriptions are source or speaker claims. Company and personal names are transliterated where official English forms remain unverified.

DAY 2 · UNIQUE GROW

The Product Is Built—Now What?

When it comes to going overseas, the bottleneck is never the first step. The real difficulty is what comes after.

When it comes to going overseas, the bottleneck is never the first step.

The first step—more and more people have already taken it: the product is launched, the team is assembled, the target market is chosen.

The real difficulty is what comes after: Where do users come from? How do you do retention? How does your brand get remembered overseas? How do you scale content? The logic of product selection and fulfillment in e-commerce is completely different from China's, and AI has rewritten the entire rulebook once again—growth is far more complex than previously thought.

There is one more thing making this situation harder: the methods that used to work are failing.

Traffic is getting more expensive, the mass-listing logic is starting to break down amid platform fragmentation, the barrier to content-driven customer acquisition is changing, and AI has rewritten the user-reach path itself. Veterans who have been going overseas for five years and new teams just entering the market face the same set of new questions.

What Day2 wants to discuss is the answers that some people have already found within this new set of questions.

May 22, 2026 Unique Awards · Shenzhen Day2, Unique Grow, AI Globalization Growth Summit.

From product to growth, from 1 to 10.

Day2 · Agenda

Keynote | 2026 AI Globalization: From "Going Out" to "Putting Down Roots"

Keynote | Digital Intelligence Future: The Biggest Certainty Variable for Enterprise Growth

Speaker: Chen Pengfei, Chief Digital Intelligence Growth Officer, Juewei Group

Roundtable 1 | Product Revolution

When the Next Generation of AI Products Is No Longer Designed for Humans

There are some AI products whose primary users are not humans but other Agents. This direction is opening up a completely different product logic—the target user has changed, the interaction method has changed, and the evaluation criteria have changed too.

Roundtable 2 | Traffic Reshuffle

From SEO to GEO: How Can Overseas Brands Intercept New Traffic in the Era of Large Models?

Getting your brand to appear in AI's answers, not just on the first page of Google—this is called GEO, and it is becoming a new required course for overseas growth. This session explains how this logic works in practice and where teams should start today.

Roundtable 3 | Cross-Border E-Commerce

How Is AI Reshaping Product Selection Logic, Live-Stream Selling and Cross-Border Fulfillment?

Every link in cross-border e-commerce is being penetrated by AI. But the gap between teams that have truly made this work and teams that have merely "added a few tools" is already widening. This session breaks down what the former are doing differently.

12:00 — 12:30

✦ Awards |《2026 Global AI 100》

The annual ranking of the most influential AI globalization companies is officially unveiled here.

Keynote | The Core of AI Implementation: Driving Full-Link Cost Reduction and Efficiency Gains Through Business

Speaker: Zhang Weili, Ecosystem Lead, Pagoda Technology Center

Roundtable 4 | AI Marketing

How Is AI Rewriting the Narrative Rules of Global Brands?

Everyone is building overseas brands, but some use AI to mass-produce content while others use AI for precise user mindshare capture. The results of these two approaches are very far apart. This session discusses how overseas brands should tell stories in the AI era and whom to tell them to.

Roundtable 5 | Infinite Studio

How Can AI Industrially Produce Global Content?

Three people, relying on AI content industrialization, simultaneously run over a dozen vertical accounts overseas. This is not a joke—it is something already happening this year. After AI rewrote the cost and efficiency of content production, both the threshold and the ceiling of content going overseas have changed.

Roundtable 6 | Growth Strategy

In the AI Era, How Can You Achieve Low-Cost Viral Growth and Scalable Replication of Overseas Users?

Customer acquisition is expensive, retention is hard, viral growth is slow—are there new solutions to these three problems in the AI era? This session discusses the teams that have truly spun up the growth flywheel with AI and how their methodologies emerged.

Roundtable 7 | Claw's Great Voyage

The Dividends and Business Opportunities Behind the Lobster Frenzy

The Agent wave has opened a real commercial window. What are the first people to turn it into a business doing? How long will this dividend last? Where is the next overseas scenario that Agents can reshape? This session breaks it down head-on.

Roundtable 8 | Cross-Border Collaboration

Global Talent Strategy and Culture Building for AI-Native Enterprises

How do you build a team—hire locals or send expatriates? How do you handle the friction of cross-cultural collaboration? This session discusses the AI companies that have truly taken off in multiple markets and how their talent strategies evolved.

Who Will Be There?

He Shan, Co-founder of Show3D; Zhou Ze'an, Founder of Biyou Technology; Joe, Founder of Halo; Wan Songling, Founder of Future Quest; Peter, Founder of 94AI; Charley, Founder of FOSHO; Alex, Founder of AllyClaw; Shen Yang, Founder of Qiyu Shuke; Liu Kun, Founder of PhotoG; Wang Weiyang, Founder of Zenkit; Kelly, Founder of Buda; Shi Yi, CEO of Thinkla; Wu Xiankun, Founder of Kuse.ai; Yin Tianming, Founder of Senluo Zhihui; Yu Beichuan, Founder of Index Gravity; Li Kejia, Founder of Botlearn; Li Shaohui, Founder of Kuaijuece; Li Yafei, Founder of Clacky; Zhang Weili, Ecosystem Lead at Pagoda Technology Center; Chen Pengfei, Chief Digital Intelligence Growth Officer at Juewei Group; Li Biao, Founder of Zhidun Technology; Chen Li from Octopus (octopus); Chen Guang, Founder of QuickCEP; Chen Ming, Founder of Nuomibao; Yang Jinsong, Founder of Future Style Intelligence; Zhang Keyi, Founder of LynxAI; Wang Jiancong, Co-founder of AhaLab; Monica Wang Shiyao; Benjamin Klingsbo, Swedish entrepreneur; Bernie; Zeneth Wong, Founder of Asia AI Startup Fund; Albert Lam, CEO of Nuoda Robotics; Anthony Aurelien Ribout, Founder of Arsk Sound & Shape Creative Brand; Winson Kwok, Founder of VenturePort investment platform; Richard Zhao, CEO of OneOneTalk AI teaching platform; Sun Haiyang, CEO of Shenzhen Bi'an Xinzhi Technology; Darren Su Peng, Co-founder of AGI Villa; Yu Yi, Senior Researcher at Tencent Research Institute; Pucs, Co-founder of No Capital; Gao Lei, User Strategy and PMF expert; Ryan Julan, Founder & CEO of Mengli Innovation; CG, Founder of Yisi Tennis Robot; Patric Yang Gang, Founder & Curator; Ark Zhang Zifeng, Founder of Spiral Inc; Noah Zeming, Founder of Tango AI; Veve Li Jingyi, Founder & CEO of SeeMe AIGC photography workflow software; Co-founder of Index Gravity (Superlinear), as well as core team members from Molian Technology, Yixuan Technology and other companies.

Registration

2026 Unique Awards · Shenzhen · Day2 Unique Grow — AI Globalization Growth Summit

Date: May 22, 2026 (Friday)

Venue: The Westin Shenzhen Nanshan (益田威斯汀酒店)

Organizer: Unique Research (非凡产研)

Free admission, application-based. Confirmation email sent upon approval.
